key_insight: A probabilistic deep learning model can forecast Alzheimer’s progression over multiple future visits while also estimating how uncertain each trajectory is.
clinical_relevance: This could help clinicians interpret not only the most likely next diagnosis, but also how confidently the model expects changes from mild cognitive impairment to dementia over time.
method: Temporal Fusion Transformer encoder with CORAL ordinal diagnosis prediction
Autoregressive Mixture Density Network for 5-year trajectories of diagnosis, CDR-SB, MMSE orientation, and hippocampal volume
Separate aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty using mixture variance and a 5-member bootstrap ensemble
evidence_signal: On ADNI, the model outperformed linear, recurrent, and transformer baselines for next-visit diagnosis prediction, and external testing on OASIS-3 showed higher epistemic uncertainty alongside higher error.
watch_item: Performance on rare progression patterns and external data may be less stable, so deployment would need careful validation before any practical use.
paper_title: Uncertainty-Aware Longitudinal Forecasting of Alzheimer's Disease Progression Using Deep Learning
